source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Nameless: the beginning of Heaven and Earth. Named: the mother of the myriad things.
Therefore, always without desire, one can observe its subtle mystery.
Always with desire, one can observe its outward manifestations.
These two come forth together yet have different names; together they are called dark.
Darkness upon darkness: the gateway to all subtleties.
When all under heaven know beauty as beauty, then ugliness is already there.
When all know good as good, then non-good is already there.

Therefore being and nonbeing give rise to each other; difficulty and ease complete each other; long and short compare with each other; high and low incline toward each other; sound and voice harmonize with each other; front and back follow one another.
Thus the sage deals with affairs without action guided by self-will,
and teaches without words. The myriad things arise, yet he does not refuse them; he gives birth to them yet does not possess them; he acts for them yet does not rely on them,
and, when the work is accomplished, does not dwell on it.
Precisely because he does not dwell on it, it does not leave him.

If worthies are not esteemed, the people will not contend; if hard-to-get goods are not prized, the people will not become thieves; if desirable things are not displayed, the people's hearts will not be disturbed.
Thus, in the sage's governance, he empties their minds and fills their bellies,
weakens their wills and strengthens their bones.
So that the wise do not dare act.
Act without action, and there is nothing that will not be governed.

The Way is hollow, yet when used it is never exhausted; so deep, it seems to be the ancestor of the myriad things. It blunts its sharpness, unties its tangles, softens its glare, and mingles with its dust; so deep, it seems to exist.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical route for travel, or a path/trail along which one goes.
Sentence Translations (English): He traveled on the road and did not lose his proper course.
Heavy rain ruined the road, and carts and horses could not pass.
He lost his way and asked for the path, and then found it.
There is an old path east of the village that leads to the river.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A practical way, method, or approach for carrying out an action or achieving a result.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Refers to a workable procedure or mode of conduct, not the cosmic Way.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; often in philosophical and instructional prose
Sentence Translations (English): If ruling a state has a proper method, then the people are secure.
In learning, what matters is to grasp the right method.
There is a sure way to win in war, and it lies in judging the situation.
In all affairs, if one loses the right method, there will be many failures.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To utter words, speak, or express something in language.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Plain verbal use, often in formal or literary prose.
Sentence Translations (English): He was unwilling to state the truth.
Everyone laughed, but he alone did not dare to speak it.
The court historian recorded it on the basis of what he had heard.
He wished to speak, but did not yet dare to do so.
Sentences: 眾人皆笑，而他獨不敢道。

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fundamental principle or reality that underlies and orders the world; the ultimate Way that can be spoken of only provisionally.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often carries a philosophical and cosmological sense beyond an ordinary path or method.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses that something is fitting, proper, or acceptable.
Sentence Translations (English): This proposal is indeed acceptable.
His words are very appropriate.
When the timely rain has come, field work is especially suitable.
This plan can certainly be carried out.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To regard as right and give assent to it.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): An act of approval or agreement.
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler approved his request.
Everyone approved it.
The lord did not approve the proposal.
Once the master approved it, the disciples followed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks ability, possibility, or permission to do something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Function word of potential or permissive force.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To judge something as wrong or blameworthy, or to reject it verbally.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often appears with objects or in evaluative statements.
Sentence Translations (English): A gentleman does not criticize another's faults.
Everyone disapproved of his proposal.
I dare to criticize it.
He takes this matter to be good; I do not dare to condemn it.
Sentences: 彼以此事為善，吾不敢非。

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Functions as a negative predicate in Classical Chinese, denying that something belongs to a class or has a stated property.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): This is the simple negative in predicative use, not the later disyllabic word 非常.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The enduring, unchanging Way.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A stable, abiding principle rather than a temporary or variable one.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To give a name to something or identify it by name.
Sentence Translations (English): The father then named him.
The child was born unnamed, and only later was it settled.
Everyone together named the mountain.
I want to name this thing.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Public renown or the standing a person or thing has among others.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Social standing as known by others.
Sentence Translations (English): He loves fame.
A gentleman values establishing a name.
Empty fame is not worth relying on.
Only after a long time did his reputation take shape.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A designation by which something is called or known.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text it is opposed to namelessness and verbal definition.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An enduring or fixed designation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Contrasts with changing or spoken names.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A philosophical notion of absence, nonexistence, or the condition of being nothing rather than something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used in speculative or metaphysical discussion, not ordinary lack.
Sentence Translations (English): The sage holds to nothingness in order to meet every change.
By contemplating nothingness, one knows the root of being.
The myriad things are born from nothingness.
If one knows that nothingness is useful, then the mind is tranquil.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates absence or lack: something is not present, possessed, or available.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks simple absence or lack, often before nouns or noun phrases.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired totality of the natural world and the cosmic order.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A fixed binomial naming the cosmic order as a whole.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

Sentence Translations (English): He saw him and told him.
I will ask him.
Everyone knows it.
It must not be disobeyed.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks motion toward a place or goal.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often occurs in fixed or formal motion expressions.
Sentence Translations (English): I shall go to Chu.
Where do you wish to go?
The envoy goes to the capital.
Tomorrow we shall go east.
additional_senses.Translation (English): to go to; to travel to

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Links a noun phrase to the following noun or noun phrase in a genitive or attributive relation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A grammatical linker, not a lexical noun.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To set something in motion or make it commence.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Denotes actual inception of an action or event.
Sentence Translations (English): When the spring wind has arrived, farm work then begins.
The king began to organize the troops.
At midnight the drums first sounded.
Before the affair begins, first set the heart right.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The point from which something starts or comes forth.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A substantive starting-point, not the verb ‘begin.’
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates existence, presence, or possession.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can mark both possession and existential presence.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The totality of created or existing things.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A comprehensive plural for all creatures and things.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A source, progenitor, or nurturing origin.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often extended metaphorically to an originating source.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, general; philosophical extension in Laozi

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a conclusion or result from what precedes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Resultative connective.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Stable, unchanging, or regular in nature.
Sentence Translations (English): The four seasons have their constancy.
The gentleman keeps to constancy.
Only by seeking constancy within change can one endure.
The statutes do not lose their regular order.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Continuously or habitually, without interruption.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks ongoing or habitual state.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, received Laozi/Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A want, craving, or wish that draws one toward something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can imply desire as a source of disturbance or partial vision in the Laozi.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, general; philosophical usage in Laozi

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a method, means, or purpose.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Common instrumental or purposive marker.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): by means of; in order to

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To look at attentively or examine in order to understand.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often means contemplative seeing, not merely casual looking.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, general; philosophical in Laozi

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person possessive or attributive marker referring back to something mentioned.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Context supplies the referent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): What is subtle, faint, or hard to grasp.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In Laozi, points to the elusive depth of reality.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An edge, limit, or outer margin.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text, the outward limit or trace of things.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Refers to something present or just mentioned.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Deictic, pointing to what is immediately under discussion.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The number 2.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Count word or numeral in classical prose.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A nominalizing or pluralizing suffix attached to a preceding noun or pronoun.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Turns the preceding expression into a thing or class of things.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Being alike, identical, or in accord.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can mark identity or mutuality.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move out from within or originate from a source.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Concrete emergence or derivation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Joins clauses or marks a relation of coordination or contrast.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Flexible connector, often with mild adversative or sequential force.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Not the same; unlike.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks distinction or disparity.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To refer to something as, or to say that it is.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Naming or predicative attribution.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Deeply hidden, obscure, or mysterious.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A depth beyond ordinary perception.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates repetition or addition.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks recurrence or intensification.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The whole set or a large number of things.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Collective sense.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An opening for entry or exit, or a figurative portal or access point.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often literal, sometimes metaphorical access.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The human realm or the whole world.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A universal totality centered on human order.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Every member of a set without exception.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Universal quantifier.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To be aware of, understand, or recognize.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Cognitive knowledge or recognition.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Possessing or referring to pleasing beauty.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here a quality used as a value-term.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a judgment or classification, treating one thing as another.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Predicative or classificatory use, not the general verb 'do'.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to take as; to regard as

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks a resulting or immediate consequence.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often points to the immediate consequence just stated.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally bad, harmful, or undesirable.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A value term opposite to good.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks that something has been completed or is by now the case.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Completion or settled state.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally good, fitting, or beneficial.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Ethical or evaluative goodness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Negates a verb, adjective, or clause.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): General verbal negation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates reciprocal relation or interaction between items.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Reciprocity or mutuality.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To produce or bring forth something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative generation, not just biological birth.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A paired contrast of difficulty and ease.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Fixed contrasting binomial.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To bring to completion, make effective, or form something fully.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Completion or mutual fulfillment.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A paired contrast of length.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Fixed contrast of measure or extent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To place side by side for comparison.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Comparative matching or weighing.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A paired contrast of rank, position, or elevation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often spatial or social hierarchy.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): high and low; above and below

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To lean, slant, or press toward one side.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Motion toward imbalance or leaning.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Audible noise, tone, or voice.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Natural or produced sound as a phenomenon.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To be in accord or produce consonance with another.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Mutual fitting or concord.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A paired contrast of position.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Spatial or temporal sequence.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To follow behind or accompany.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often implies accompanying sequence.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a conclusion from what has been stated.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Conclusive connective phrase.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person of extraordinary wisdom and moral insight.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): An idealized wise ruler or exemplar.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To occupy a place or manage an affair.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here manages or handles conduct.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A thing to be done, an action, or a matter under consideration.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Broad term for affairs or actions.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move on foot or carry out an action.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In context, to practice or carry out.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Spoken language or utterance.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Verbal expression.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Instruction or doctrine communicated to others.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often moral or doctrinal instruction.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move into action, emerge, or begin operation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): An action coming into being.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A locative or resultant particle indicating a state or place.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often marks a resultant state or location.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To decline, disclaim, or not take on a response.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here, not shirking the needs of things.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take credit for or lean upon something as support.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Dependence or self-assurance in virtue of something.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A completed accomplishment or service.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often an accomplished result or merit.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative form used especially in literary style.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Literary negation, often in set phrases.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take up residence or hold a position.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Taking credit or remaining in a place/state.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A discourse particle used to introduce or emphasize the following statement.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Rhythmic or exclamatory introductory particle.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks exclusiveness or limitation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Restrictive sense.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To go away or disappear.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Movement away or loss of presence.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To prize or put high value on.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Positive valuation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person of merit or moral excellence.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A person considered fit for office or esteem.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To bring about or let something happen.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative use.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The ordinary people as a social group.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Collective subject of governance.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To fight for priority or argue over something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Conflict or competitive struggle.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To regard as important or precious.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): High valuation, often material or moral.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Hard to obtain, achieve, or deal with.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks scarcity or difficulty.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To acquire or receive.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Acquisition or attainment.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Property, valuables, or trade goods.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Material objects of value.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person who steals or the act of stealing.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Criminal taking; in context, not theft by office-holders.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To look at or perceive with the eyes; by extension, to notice.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Perceptual seeing, often implying exposure to sight.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The seat of thought, feeling, and intention.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Collective inner disposition of the people.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Lack of order, calm, or proper arrangement.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Mental or social disorder.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The activity or system of governing and administering.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Public administration or government action.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To empty out, reduce, or leave free of content.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means to empty or leave unfilled.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The inner faculty of thought, emotion, and intention.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often both intellect and emotion.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To put in content or increase to fullness.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Opposite of emptying.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The stomach or abdominal area.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Physical body sense.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To make less strong, forceful, or intense.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative reduction in strength.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A fixed intention or determination.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Mental purpose or ambition.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To make stronger or more robust.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative strengthening.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The hard structural parts of the body.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Concrete body part; in context, physical vigor.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person skilled in knowledge and judgment.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A person characterized by intelligence or wisdom.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To have the courage or audacity to do something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Ability plus boldness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A sentence-final particle used to soften, affirm, or complete an utterance.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks finality or assertion in classical prose.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a consequence or result.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Consequence marker.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Not full; spacious or hollow.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here the sense is emptiness or open spaciousness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The employment or function of something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can denote both employing and practical utility.

source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Without a name, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with a name, it is the mother of the myriad things.
